reviews.review:
Great game for people who feel guilty about who they have to kill in games like Vermintide, but have been sufficiently educated by Starship Troopers to understand that going underground to kill bugs and bring back piles of shiney ore is essentially doing the Lord's work.

The only good bug is a ____ bug.

So you take Minecraft's addictive mining and put it together with TF2's wacky hats and then L4D2's fantastic multiplayer experiance , then you mix it up with cool and refined mechanics and you get Deep Rock Galactic .
Most games have so many weapons but said weapons become almost worthless when you get stronger ones , some games have an upgrade sistem but it becomes boring after getting all the upgrades on that weapon , DRG fixes those issues by having just the right about of weapons and they have MODS rather then UPGRADES , you can not have all mods on a weapon forcing you to choose , "Do you want more Ammo or more Damage ?" by doing this you add creativity and replayability because in one mission you can have all the ammo in the world and in another mission you can wipe out everything with high caliber rounds .
There are 9 mission types , each one is very unique making them not blend in , further more they have a chance to have modifires forcing the player to adapt otherwise they will fail , speaking of adapting , there are biomes with hazards and gimics the player can take advantage of like the exploding mushrooms from Magma Core can be used to blow up swarms
The game takes you back to the good ol days when you had to play the game to get cosmetics rather then gamble , its seasonal battle passes and cosmetic trees we're made to make the updates themed and it was a huge success due to said battle passes being free and you never have to worry about missing out .
However like everything in life , this game is not perfect , new players will have a harder time then older players because they need to work to unlock everything , overclocks are random and thats about it .
Overall rating 9.9/10 would Rock & Stone again .
